# Concordia's Thursday Report, 23 May 2002 — photo caption

Source: https://archive.org/details/thursday-report-2002-may-23
Transcribed 2026-09-07 from `Thursday-Report-2002-May-23_djvu.txt` (120,806 bytes).
The whole issue was grepped; this caption is its only Kanawana mention. There is no
accompanying article — the awards got a photograph and a caption that year.

---

> SEAMAN AWARDS FOR COMMUNITY LEADERSHIP: Every year, the A. Ross Seaman Leadership Award
> goes to students in applied human sciences at Concordia, Dawson College, and several other
> community programs in memory of an outstanding teacher.
>
> This year's winners, honoured at a ceremony March 20 at Dawson are, left to right: Jacinthe
> Morsani (Leisure Sciences, Concordia), Kimberley Jackson (Concordia), winner of a
> scholarship from the sale of a book called *Tapestry of Adulthood: Women's Reflections*;
> Ruxandra Vlad (Human Relations, Concordia), (behind her) Shawn Jaffray (Therapeutic
> Recreation, Concordia), Justin Desforges (Kamp Kanawana), Anna Tafuto (Dawson), and
> Elizabeth Sweeney (YWCA). The second scholarship winner, Donna O'Bomsawin (Concordia), was
> not present for the photo.

---

## Notes on reading this

**The constituency list moves.** 2001 has the YMCA; 2002 has the **YWCA** and no YMCA. Kamp
Kanawana is in both. Whether the 2002 caption is a substitution, an error, or a genuine year
in which the YMCA award went unclaimed cannot be told from the caption.

**The ceremony moved to Dawson** (20 March 2002). The 2001 evening's venue is not stated in
that year's article.

**A second, separately funded scholarship** is visible here for the first time in this
project's sources: two winners drawn from the sale of *Tapestry of Adulthood: Women's
Reflections*, which is a funding mechanism distinct from the auction evening.
